title_original: Avengers: Doomsday has brought with it more ‘Marvel homework’ than ever. That’s just as it should be
excerpt_original: Working out where returning hero Steve Rogers has been is only one of the multiversal puzzles fans must now get their heads around – which is catnip for the connoisseurs The cinema release of Avengers: Doomsday is now roughly three weeks away and, judging by the final trailer ,…

blocks.text: T he cinema release of Avengers: Doomsday is now roughly three weeks away and, judging by the final trailer , we’re living in the one timeline where every loose end Marvel has left dangling for years is now worth tugging on. Even the ones we thought the studio had tied up rather nicely. Ever since it became apparent that Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers would be returning in the new film, along with next year’s sequel Avengers: Secret Wars, fans have been asking themselves: where exactly has he been all this time? Now, thanks to the latest footage, we’re beginning to get an idea, and we might also be starting to pick up clues as to why Doctor Doom would take an interest in his new postcode.

One of the most startling aspects of the new trailer is the arrival of the Fantastic Four, led by Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards, on Rogers’ front lawn. We’ve known since the finale of Avengers: Endgame that Steve used Tony Stark’s newly discovered time-travelling tech to go back to the 1940s and live out his life with Peggy Carter during the events of that film – but until recently it seemed most likely that happened in good old Earth-616, the main Marvel Cinematic Universe continuity.

Then there was the new final scene in Endgame: Encore , in which Loki turned up to offer the happy couple some kind of nebulous “help”. Fans have been theorising for a while that because the god of mischief is now holding the multiverse together (thanks to the events of season two of Loki ) he might be offering them the chance to shift into an alternative reality, for reasons unknown. That idea looks a little more plausible now that Richards and co have turned up at the lovers’ house. Did Steve and Peggy somehow make it to Earth-828, the retro-futurist reality introduced in last year’s The Fantastic Four: First Steps ? And is this one of the reasons why Doom is so angry with them?

blocks.text: Stay with me here. We already know, thanks to a mid-credits scene in Encore , that the multiverse is collapsing due to a series of incursions between different universes across thousands of worlds. Might moving Steve and Peggy into another reality have helped trigger one on Earth-828? Doomsday co-director Joe Russo has spoken about how this new version of Doom is suffering from the loss of a child, which might explain his anger towards the universe (or multiverse) in general. Have Steve’s reality-shifting antics, his decision to try to find himself a life away from heroism, created the circumstances that have led others to suffer? “All of you have lived stolen lives,” says Doom in the new footage. “But now you must give them back.” The trailer then cuts to Thor and Scott Lang (Ant-Man) with their daughters.

links.text: Doomsday co-director Joe Russo has spoken

blocks.text: Thor’s adoptive daughter, Love, is an intriguing choice for the trailer to focus on. At the end of Thor: Love and Thunder , Christian Bale’s Gorr uses his one wish to bring her back from the dead, and Thor takes her in. Now here’s another father who’s lost a child, telling the Avengers they have to give back the lives he says they stole. And then there’s the child Doom has already paid a visit. In a First Steps credits scene , Sue Storm goes to fetch her son Franklin a book and comes back to find a certain sinister supervillain kneeling in front of him in the living room. We know the boy has godlike powers, having brought his mother back from the dead. It’s worth asking what a man in Doom’s position might want from him, especially when he’s lost a child of his own.

blocks.text: One of the biggest criticisms of Marvel over the past few years has been the sheer amount of required viewing everyone has to get through – from Disney+ shows to post-credits teasers and new footage tucked into rereleases – just to be able to work out what’s going on. And yet here we are, three weeks from Doomsday, checking the custody arrangements at the end of a four-year-old Thor film, combing the multiversal electoral roll for Captain America, and desperately trying to remind ourselves why the ruler of Latveria turned up in full armour for story time. Which of course is exactly what should be happening this close to the release of a new Avengers movie: Marvel reminding us that sometimes, the right kind of homework is actually worth completing.
